title: ‘We are not alone:’ Coalition of UFO whistleblowers call on Trump to let them publicly reveal secrets
text:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

The world’s most prominent UFO whistleblowers have formed an unprecedented coalition to ask President Trump to waive their government nondisclosure agreements — which they say are preventing them from sharing what they know about extraterrestrial life with the American public.

Dylan Borland, David Grusch and Matthew Brown say they accumulated the information while working in highly classified government programs and are legally barred from discussing it publicly without White House intervention.

“For the first time in history you have a direct public plea, not private . . . to the president of the United States, to have their NDAs waived and have them protected, so they can disclose what they know to the American population, because they feel like it’s that important that everyone should be entitled to know that we’re not alone,” filmmaker and disclosure advocate James Fox told The Post.

“You’ve got some heavyweight whistleblowers willing to reveal what they know. All they need is immunity from the president. Just the stroke of a pen. He’s got the authority to do it,” said Fox.

Matthew Brown was an independent contractor for the defense industry and came forward on the Weaponized Podcast in early 2026 to reveal details about an alleged secret government program called Immaculate Constellation which collects data on UFOs from across the government.

“The NDAs I signed prohibit me from publicly disclosing classified information obtained through my national security work without prior written government authorization, and that obligation lasts for life,” Brown said.

He added: “President Trump has the opportunity to uproot the source of deep-state corruption, reset international relations, and lead humanity into a new era of awareness and discovery by disclosing one simple fact: we are not alone.”

David Grusch, an Air Force officer, was an intelligence officer at the National Geospatial Intelligence Agency and the National Reconnaissance Office, testified to Congress in 2023 that the US government has operated secret UFO crash retrieval programs for decades.

“Mr. President, give us the authorization and we’re ready to go,” Grusch said in a video released by Fox.

Grusch said evidence he has seen is jaw-dropping.

“This included photographs and video of the [recovery] operations including the craft and the non-human occupants. And I’ve seen this evidence with my own two eyes,” he said.

“I am prepared to provide a full historical accounting to the National Security Council . . . and the White House Chief of Staff and make any supporting public statements that are authorized.”

Dylan Borland, an Air Force veteran, testified to Congress in 2024 that he witnessed a massive triangular UFO hovering and maneuvering over a NASA hangar for several minutes before it zoomed off into the sky in the flash of an eye.

He wants to come forward and share his full story with the public — but warned he and his compatriots would need direct approval from Trump to share any corroborating classified evidence.

“Disclosure has to come from [President Trump]. He needs to rip the Band-Aid off himself and needs to go out there and confirm we’re not alone. We’ve recovered materials and entities — biologics,”  Borland told The Post.

Rep. Eric Burlison (R-Mo.), who supports the group of whistleblowers, lauded the administration and stated Trump has the chance to be the most consequential leader in modern times.

“He’s already demonstrated that he’s willing to be more transparent to the American people than any president in American history,” Burlison told The Post.

“Each of these tranches of releases we have had — even just one of the documents in one of the tranches — would’ve been a monumental moment in UAP history prior to the Trump administration.”

The administration announced a new legal waiver allowing current and former government personnel to report UFO and alien-related information to the federal government — but only through the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters, not for disclosure to the public.

Rep. Anna Paulina Luna (R-Fla.), who chairs the House Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets, said her focus has been on protecting whistleblowers rather than pushing for public release.

“Heading up the Declass Task Force I quickly discovered a lot of these whistleblowers were scared to go public in fear of retribution, so I made efforts to secure whistleblower protections as a top priority,” she told The Post. “We are hoping with these new measures in place in people will feel safer to come forward.”
